questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I rent a flat from the Rebhalde Cooperative at Schulhausstrasse 8 in St. Gallen, and I signed the lease in June 2022. There was never any agreement that the rent would go up in set steps every year or so. Nothing of that kind is in my contract.

What the contract does have is a clause saying the rent follows the Swiss consumer price index. I remember Mr Tom Frei pointing it out to me when I signed, saying it was standard for the cooperative. As far as I can tell, this increase is simply that clause being applied.

On 1 March 2026 I received a letter from Mr Frei telling me that my rent of CHF 1640 will rise to CHF 1675 a month. It's not a huge jump, I know, but I'd like to understand whether they are calculating it correctly, because my colleague Sam Bucher, who also has an index clause with a different landlord, says his increase was much smaller. I've also heard that there are rules about how often and by how much this kind of increase can be passed on, and I have no idea whether those were followed in my case.

Could you tell me whether it makes sense to have this checked, and if so, how I should go about it?

Kind regards,
Alice Bachmann
